title: Eventual stationarity of finite diagonal cycle and boundary towers
statement: Under the finite diagonal tail hypotheses, the cycle and boundary subobjects of the canonical tower are eventually constant at every bidegree.

proof.text: Use finiteCycle_formula and finiteBoundary_alphaKernel for the canonical towers. Fix p,q and choose a lower cocone-isomorphism bound a on degree p+q and an upper zero bound b on degree p+q+1. Set r=max(toNat(p-a),toNat(b-p-2)). For every t>=r the source D(p+2+t,q-1-t) of incomingAlphaIter t is zero; its image is zero and the cycle formula gives Z t=ker(original f).

Reuse the existing private alphaIter_cocone theorem through a proof-only import all of Sheaf.CategoryTheory.FiniteCoconeLimitBoundaries; it telescopes alphaIter t against the cocone transition equations, including all index transports. For t>=r the endpoint p-t is at most a, so its cocone map is an isomorphism. Postcomposition with this isomorphism and the endpoint transport preserves kernels; hence ker(alphaIter t) is the kernel of the cocone map at p transported from D(p,q). The finite boundary formula therefore makes B t the fixed initial-g image of this kernel. The cycle and boundary formulas also hold at r, proving both eventual equalities.

proof_origin.place: Tag 011T and shifted Tag 0AMJ give the finite formulas; the diagonal-tail cocone argument is an agent-written generalization of the finite-filtration argument of Tag 012W. Returned-delivery repair reuses the existing cocone iteration helper from FiniteCoconeLimitBoundaries instead of proving it again.

lean.statement: theorem finiteCocone_stationary {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (X : BigradedExactCouple C 0) (A : ∀ n : ℤ, X.AlphaColimit n) (hA : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, (∀ P : ℤ, P ≤ a → IsIso ((A n).ι P)) ∧ (∀ P : ℤ, b ≤ P → IsZero (X.D P (n - P)))) : ∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, r ≤ t → X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z t p q = X.cycleBoundaryTower.Z r p q ∧ X.cycleBoundaryTower.B t p q = X.cycleBoundaryTower.B r p q
